﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar.﴾ This is an address to the Prophet (ﷺ). Al-Kawthar takes the form of the intensive pattern (*fa'awthar*, with the *tha'* added) from *kathra* (abundance). There are seven opinions on its interpretation:

The first is that it is the Basin (*hawd*) of the Prophet (ﷺ).

The second is that it is the abundant good that God gave him [*lahu*] in this world and the Hereafter. This was said by Ibn Abbas, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr followed him. If it is objected that the river in Paradise is also part of the good God gave him, then the meaning is general.

The third is that al-Kawthar is the Qur'an.

The fourth is that it is the abundance of companions and followers.

The fifth is that it is the Tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness).

The sixth is that it is the intercession (*shafa'a*).

The seventh is that it is a light God placed in his heart.

There is no doubt that God gave him all of these things. However, the correct view is that al-Kawthar refers to the Basin, because of the authentic hadith in which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Do you know what al-Kawthar is? It is a river God has given me, and it is the Basin, whose vessels are as numerous as the stars of the sky."

﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice.﴾ On this verse there are five opinions:

The first is that he was commanded to pray in general and to sacrifice the offerings (*hady*) and the sacrificial animals (*dahaya*).

The second is that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to sacrifice before the Eid prayer, so he was commanded to pray and then sacrifice. According to this view, the intended meaning is to delay the slaughter of the sacrificial animals until after the prayer.

The third is that the disbelievers used to pray with *mukaa'* and *tasdiya* (whistling and clapping, the Arabic words *mukaa'* and *tasdiya* being the terms here) and slaughtered for the idols. So God said to His Prophet (ﷺ): "Pray to your Lord alone and sacrifice to Him," that is, for His countenance and not for anyone else. According to this view, it is a command to affirm the Tawhid and to sincerity (*ikhlas*).

The fourth is that the meaning of *inhar* (sacrifice) is: place your right hand upon your left at your chest (*sadr*) during the prayer. According to this view, it derives from *nahr*, which means the chest.

The fifth is that its meaning is: raise your hands at your chest (*nahr*) when beginning the prayer.

﴿Indeed, the one who hates you is the one cut off.﴾ *Al-Shani'* is the one who hates, and *al-shana'an* means enmity. This verse was revealed concerning al-As ibn Wa'il, and it was said it was about Abu Jahl, as a rebuttal of him when he said: "Muhammad is *abtar*," that is, he has no male offspring; when he dies we will be rid of him and his affair will end with his death. So God informed that this disbeliever is the *abtar*, even if he has children, because he is cut off (*mabtur*) from the mercy of God, that is, cut off from it. Moreover, when he is mentioned, he is mentioned only with a curse. By contrast, the Prophet (ﷺ), his remembrance endures until the end of time; he is raised up on the pulpits and the minarets, his name is joined with the remembrance of God, and the believers from his time until the Day of Resurrection are his followers, and so he is like their father.
